chunks: Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Arzami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) led the people in prayer while in a state of impurity, and it was the Dhuhr prayer. Then he entered, and his caller went out announcing that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had prayed while impure, so re-perform it, and let the witness convey to the absent one.

This is a rare report (khabar shadh) contrary to all other reports, and its ruling is that action is not taken upon it, given that within it is that which invalidates it, namely that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) performed a obligatory prayer while impure, unaware of that, and we are assured of that by the indication of his infallibility (peace be upon him). And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn mentioned, saying: I heard a group of our scholars saying: There is no re-performance required for what is prayed aloud, and re-performance is required for what he led them in praying that was not prayed aloud. And likewise, if a man leads them in prayer and then it becomes clear that he was not of their sect, there is no re-performance required for any of the prayers they performed behind him.

key_terms.شَاذٌّ: Rare/Anomalous (a report contrary to established norms)
key_terms.غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ: While impure (not in a state of ritual purity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on re-performing prayer if the Imam prayed while impure or from a different sect?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this report of Imam Ali praying in a state of minor impurity as a rare (shadh) exception, arguing that the Imam's infallibility ('ismah) precludes simple negligence, thus the prayer is valid but not the standard practice. The text further clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between prayers offered aloud (jahr) and silently (ikhfa), noting that only the latter requires re-performance if the Imam's impurity is discovered, while maintaining the validity of the congregation's prayer even if the Imam belongs to a different sect.
